title: Receptive-field remapping and trans-saccadic space updating.
abstract: Since its discovery, perisaccadic receptive-field (RF) remapping-the shift of RFs around the time of saccades-has inspired many studies exploring its origins, characteristics, and functional implications. We review recent developments leading to a circuit model that links spatiotemporal properties of remapping to functional requirements of trans-saccadic visual stability. The model uses center/surround connections to store a stimulus' retinal position as a population activity. This activity profile is shifted backward (against the saccade) as a wave by directional connections gated by the corollary discharge of the saccade command. When the accumulative backward shift of the population activity equals the saccade magnitude (equivalent to forward RF remapping of the same magnitude), the pre-saccadic retinal position is updated to the correct post-saccadic position. The model explains translational mislocalization for stimuli flashed around saccades as imperfect updating. The model is equivalent to the classic head-direction model, suggesting a general strategy of neural computation.

title: Unique local gradient-based functional fingerprints enable precisely identifying individual infants over ages.
abstract: Brain functional connectivity (FC) exhibits individualized patterns that can serve as reliable "fingerprints" for identifying individual adults. However, the rapid and complex development of the infant brain poses significant challenges in establishing individualized, developmentally-robust functional fingerprints during infancy. In this study, we introduce a novel approach that captures fine-grained local gradients of FC derived from functional MRI, enabling precise characterization of unique subject-specific FC patterns. Our method achieved approximately 99% individual identification accuracy across longitudinal scans spanning infancy in 103 infants, substantially outperforming conventional connectome-based fingerprinting, which achieved approximately 70% accuracy. Importantly, these local gradient-based functional fingerprints, predominantly localized within association and sensory networks, were also modestly but significantly associated with infant cognitive performance. Together, these findings support the existence of individualized functional fingerprints that are stable across dynamic early brain development, offering new insights into the early development of functional individuality and its cognitive relevance.

title: Separating neurodevelopmental and psychiatric services: clinical hazard?
journal: The British journal of psychiatry : the journal of mental science
abstract: Neurodevelopmental and psychiatric disorders differ in onset and course but comorbidity between groupings is high. Diagnostically siloed services risk fragmented care, misdiagnosis, inefficiency and clinical risk. Such services also deskill clinicians and intensify waiting list pressures and budget competition. We propose more person-centric systems to reduce risk and improve outcomes.

title: Autocrine feedback maintains homeostatic neuropeptide expression in a peptidergic hub neuron.
abstract: Neuronal circuits sustain stable function by self-regulating their gene expression and neurosecretion. Patterns for autocrine feedback by neuropeptides are widespread across nervous systems, but how they contribute to neuronal homeostasis is less well understood. Here, we identify an autocrine homeostatic mechanism in a C. elegans peptidergic hub neuron. FLP-1 neuropeptide release activates the inhibitory receptor DMSR-7 on the AVK hub neurons to self-regulate flp-1 transcription, dense-core vesicle accumulation, and peptide secretion. We show that a parallel PDF-1/PDFR-1 pathway drives flp-1 expression, establishing a "push-and-pull" peptidergic feedback on the AVK neurons. AVK's peptidergic output also depends on the number of FLP-1 peptides encoded in its precursor, revealing a dosage mechanism in behavioral regulation. Moreover, flp-1 expression coordinates transcript levels of additional neuropeptides in AVK. These findings uncover FLP-1 as a self-regulating homeostatic controller within a peptidergic hub neuron and fit a model where precursor-encoded redundancy supports stable yet adaptable circuit states.

title: A Clearance-Repair-Activation Framework for Alzheimer's Disease: A Perspective and Validation Roadmap.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a heterogeneous clinicobiological syndrome involving impaired protein clearance, neuroinflammation, synaptic and cellular injury, network dysfunction, and progressive functional decline. Amyloid-directed antibodies provide an evidence-based treatment backbone for selected patients with early symptomatic AD, but adjunctive strategies may be needed to address other disease mechanisms. This Perspective proposes a clearance-repair-activation framework for hypothesis-driven research. Clearance includes established pharmacological treatment and risk management as well as investigational drainage approaches; lymphaticovenous anastomosis (LVA) and deep cervical lymphaticovenous anastomosis (dcLVA) are considered only as research options within this broader domain. Repair includes neural stem-cell (NSC), induced pluripotent stem-cell-derived, engineered-cell, and secretome-based strategies, for which AD evidence remains predominantly preclinical. Activation encompasses invasive and non-invasive stimulation, sensory entrainment, neurofeedback, brain-computer interface (BCI) monitoring, and cognitive rehabilitation; BCI is positioned mainly as an experimental monitoring and adaptive rehabilitation platform. We define falsifiable links between clearance and repair readiness and between repair markers and activation responsiveness, consider adaptive and parallel alternatives to fixed sequencing, and integrate disease stage, heterogeneity, regulation, and combination-trial design. Informatics is limited to trial infrastructure and safety governance. The validation roadmap specifies success criteria, stop rules, interaction testing, clinically meaningful outcomes, and long-term surveillance.

title: Aging and False Memories: Comparing Effects of Item-Relatedness and List Position.
abstract: Evidence from classic serial position curves suggests that semantic and phonological false memories traditionally arise from presumed long- and short-term memory stores, respectively. However, research challenges this distinction, finding semantic and phonological false memories across memory stores and list positions. The present study tested whether semantic and phonological false memories reflect distinct or shared mechanisms and whether these patterns differ with age. Younger (YAs) and older (OAs) adults completed a modified Deese-Roediger-McDermott paradigm in both recall (Experiments 1 and 2) and item recognition (Experiment 3), manipulating semantic and phonological similarity across list position. During recall, although OAs recalled fewer items than YAs, both groups generated more phonological than semantic false memories. During recognition, both groups had higher hit rates for phonological than semantic items and lower false alarm rates for the phonological compared to the semantic condition. Across all experiments, both groups made semantic and phonological false memories from all sublist positions, challenging notions of strictly separated memory stores. Importantly, irrespective of test format, there were no age-related differences in false memory patterns. Together, these findings challenge traditional views of memory organization and suggest that shared cognitive processes across age group and list composition underlie semantic and phonological false memories.

title: Efficacy of Levetiracetam Combined with Sodium Valproate (Oral) in the Treatment of Senile Epilepsy and Its Effects on Cognitive Function, Inflammatory Factors and Neurotransmitters.
abstract: To evaluate the clinical efficacy of levetiracetam combined with oral sodium valproate in elderly patients with epilepsy and to assess its effects on cognitive function, inflammatory markers, and neurotransmitter levels. Seventy elderly patients with epilepsy treated between January and December 2021 were randomly assigned to a study group receiving levetiracetam plus sodium valproate or a control group receiving sodium valproate alone, with 35 patients in each group. Seizure frequency and duration, cognitive function assessed by the Montreal Cognitive Assessment, serum inflammatory factors including tumor necrosis factor alpha and interleukin six, neurotransmitters including serotonin and dopamine, and overall clinical efficacy were compared between groups after treatment. Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics were comparable between the two groups. After treatment, seizure frequency and seizure duration were significantly reduced in the combination therapy group compared with the control group. Montreal Cognitive Assessment scores were significantly higher in the combination group. Serum tumor necrosis factor alpha and interleukin six levels were significantly decreased, while serotonin and dopamine levels were significantly increased in the study group. The total clinical effective rate in the combination therapy group was significantly higher than that in the control group, and all differences reached statistical significance. Levetiracetam combined with sodium valproate demonstrated superior comprehensive efficacy in the treatment of senile epilepsy. This regimen effectively improved seizure control, cognitive function, inflammatory status, and neurotransmitter balance, supporting its value as a reliable therapeutic option for elderly patients with epilepsy under routine clinical conditions and standardized hospital treatment protocols.

title: Early infiltration of ischemia-conditioned Tregs attenuates BBB damage via suppressing neutrophil extracellular traps in ischemic stroke.
abstract: Regulatory T cells (Tregs) modulate myeloid cells but are absent early after ischemic stroke when neutrophil infiltration peaks. Whether promoting their early infiltration into the brain as an introduced niche could modulate the cerebral immune micromilieu remains unknown. Here, we show that splenic Tregs at day 5 post-MCAO (ischemia-conditioned Tregs, ICTregs) exhibit enhanced adhesion. Transferred ICTregs infiltrate the infarcted area early, alter brain cellular composition, reduce neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) and preserve blood-brain barrier (BBB) integrity during the acute phase. Mechanistically, integrin α4 anchors ICTregs to cerebral venous endothelium, and ICTreg Annexin A1 interacts with neutrophil Dectin-1 to suppress NETs. The transcription factor Ikzf2 is critical for ICTreg induction, and modulating Ikzf2 enables Sham Tregs to acquire early brain-homing capacity. These findings offer valuable insights into the neuroprotective function of ICTregs in the early stage of ischemic stroke and identify engineered-Tregs target for optimizing the brain-immune ecosystem for neural protection.

title: The ENL-USP7 complex regulates HIV latency through BRD4 protein stabilization.
abstract: HIV persistence in CD4+ T cells and brain microglia is maintained by host mechanisms that enforce viral latency. We identify ENL and the deubiquitinase USP7 as a host complex that sustains HIV latency. Pharmacologic inhibition or genetic loss of ENL reactivated latent HIV. Proteomic analyses revealed an ENL-USP7-BRD4 regulatory axis associated with latency maintenance, where USP7 maintained BRD4 protein stability. Targeted USP7 degradation using PROTAC induced latency reversal and destabilized BRD4. Chromatin immunoprecipitation studies showed that ENL was required for USP7 and BRD4 occupancy at the HIV nuc-1 region but not at the 5' long terminal repeat. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing further implicated this pathway in HIV persistence within the central nervous system. Importantly, degradation of either ENL or USP7 reactivated latent HIV in resting CD4+ T cells and brain microglia from individuals receiving antiretroviral therapy. These findings identify the ENL-USP7-BRD4 axis as a therapeutically actionable mechanism sustaining HIV latency and viral reservoirs.

title: Fanconi anemia pathway disruption drives lomustine sensitivity in glioma.
abstract: Therapeutic options for progressive glioblastoma remain limited, with chlorethyl-cyclohexyl-nitrosourea (CCNU, lomustine) among the approved treatments. Beyond MGMT gene promoter methylation, molecular determinants of CCNU sensitivity or resistance are ill- defined. We employed genome-wide functional knockout screening using the CRISPR-Cas9 technology to identify and subsequently validate modulators of response to CCNU in experimental glioma. We established an immunocompetent glioma mouse model to enable functional interrogation of Fanconi anemia pathway (FA) genes in tumor growth and synthetic lethal interactions in vivo using the RCAS/tv-a somatic gene delivery system. Multiple FA pathway members recurrently emerged as potent synthetic lethal interactors of CCNU treatment. In vivo knockdown of Fancm accelerated tumor onset and significantly increased CCNU sensitivity. Consistently, FA pathway inhibition enhanced CCNU efficacy across in vitro, ex vivo and in vivo models. Together, these findings identify FA pathway components as key synthetic lethal interactors of CCNU response and reveal a therapeutically actionable vulnerability in glioblastoma.

title: Description of a visuospatial mislocation symptom in dementia with Lewy Bodies.
Evaluation of the efficacy of oral propranolol combined with pulsed dye laser versus monotherapy with oral propranolol in the treatment of mixed infantile hemangiomas.
abstract: Oral propranolol is first-line for problematic infantile hemangiomas (IHs) but often leaves superficial residual lesions. This study assessed the efficacy and safety of adding pulsed dye laser (PDL) to propranolol versus propranolol alone for mixed IHs. This single-center retrospective cohort study included children with mixed IHs treated from January 2020 to September 2024, assigned to oral propranolol alone or with PDL. VESS (Vascular Density, Color Intensity, Texture Change) scores at 3 months, Achauer grade ≥ 4 at 1, 3, and 6 months, and regression metrics at 6 months were measured. Safety, parent-reported outcomes, treatment duration, and 12-month sequelae were also recorded. A total of 247 children were included (132 propranolol, 115 combination). The combination group had lower VESS scores at 3 months (all P < 0.010). Achauer grade ≥ 4 was more frequent at all time points (40.87% vs. 22.73% at 1 month, P = 0.002). Area reduction (75.66% vs. 70.75%, P < 0.001), thickness reduction (P = 0.024), and colorimetric ΔE (P = 0.003) were greater. Superficial erythema resolution improved (P = 0.002) with similar deep mass volume reduction. Satisfaction with color improvement (P < 0.001) and quality of life (P < 0.001), and shorter treatment duration (5.79 vs. 6.55 months, P = 0.007) favored the combined group. Recurrence (2.61% vs. 9.85%, P = 0.041) and residual telangiectasia (5.22% vs. 12.88%, P = 0.039) were lower. Transient purpura occurred only with PDL (22.61% vs. 0%, P < 0.001); other events were comparable. Adding PDL to oral propranolol significantly improves superficial clearance and aesthetic outcomes, accelerates global improvement, and reduces long-term recurrence and residual telangiectasia in mixed IHs.

title: Taking a clinical history in adolescents and adults presenting with seizures or epilepsy.
journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
abstract: Despite advances in EEG, neuroimaging, and other diagnostic technologies, a carefully obtained clinical history remains the cornerstone of diagnosis, classification, and treatment planning. However, structured guidance on history-taking that integrates state-of-the-art evidence and the updated 2025 International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE) seizure classification is limited. We performed a review of evidence published between January 2000 and April 2026, supplemented by landmark earlier studies, ILAE position papers, and National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) guidelines. Evidence was synthesized to develop a practical framework for obtaining and interpreting the clinical history in adolescents and adults presenting with a first seizure, recurrent seizures, or established epilepsy. We present a structured approach that follows the sequence of a clinical consultation, encompassing the presenting complaint, detailed event reconstruction, semiology, collateral witness accounts, smartphone video recordings, seizure triggers and temporal patterns, past medical history, medication review, family history, social factors, and safety issues. We discuss the diagnostic value of individual history elements, practical strategies for distinguishing epileptic seizures from functional/dissociative seizures and syncope, and the contribution of history-taking to seizure classification under the updated 2025 ILAE framework. We also summarize clinically relevant risk factors, comorbidities, and management implications that influence diagnostic accuracy and individualized care. Practical diagnostic questionnaires are provided to facilitate differential diagnosis and seizure classification, particularly for clinicians without specialist epilepsy expertise. A systematic clinical history, obtained from the individual and eyewitnesses and complemented by video recordings when available, remains the single most important diagnostic tool in epilepsy. Structured history-taking improves diagnostic accuracy, reduces misdiagnosis, supports accurate seizure classification, guides appropriate investigations, and provides the foundation for personalized management. This practical framework offers an evidence-based approach that can be readily incorporated into routine clinical practice and education across diverse healthcare settings.

title: Biomarker-guided immunotherapies for primary CNS tumors.
abstract: Refined immunotherapeutic modalities for the treatment of primary central nervous system (CNS) tumors - vaccines, virotherapies, immune checkpoint inhibitors, and cell therapies - are starting to show efficacy in selected patients with primary CNS tumors. Still most patients do not derive a meaningful clinical benefit, despite evidence of biological activity. While the unique immunosuppressive environment of the CNS, cellular heterogeneity and brain borders prohibiting access present substantial challenges for effective treatment, there is a need to define robust biomarkers for response to immunotherapies. As immunotherapies critically depend on multiple tumor intrinsic as well as host factors, this task is substantially more challenging than defining biomarkers for response to targeted therapies. Recent advances in biomarker identification and characterization for immunotherapies have opened new avenues for precision immunotherapy approaches. This review examines the current state of biomarker-guided immunotherapy for primary CNS tumors, focusing on key biomarkers including immunogenic antigens, HLA ligandomics, tumor immune microenvironment characteristics, cell-free DNA, tumor mutational burden, and T cell populations in tumor tissue, blood, and cerebrospinal fluid. We discuss how these biomarkers can guide the selection and optimization of immunotherapeutic strategies including cancer vaccines, T cell therapy, and immune checkpoint inhibitors particularly for glioblastoma, and highlight current challenges and future directions in the field.

title: [Not Available].
abstract: a pesar de ser un fármaco altamente eficaz para el tratamiento de la esquizofrenia resistente al tratamiento (ERT), la clozapina continúa siendo subutilizada. Este estudio tiene como objetivo evaluar los patrones de prescripción de Clozapina en pacientes ambulatorios de un hospital especializado en psiquiatría de Argentina. Métodos: este estudio observacional descriptivo retrospectivo de corte transversal incluyó pacientes adultos con diagnóstico de esquizofrenia que realizan tratamiento ambulatorio en nuestra institución. Los datos fueron recolectados mediante la revisión de historias clínicas en el período noviembre 2024-enero 2025. Los análisis estadísticos incluyeron estadísticas descriptivas, pruebas t pareadas, correlaciones de Pearson y regresión múltiple. la muestra incluyó 199 pacientes y tuvo una edad media de 36 años (DE: 6,6). El 75,4 % recibía medicación concomitante; el uso previo de antipsicóticos inyectables de acción prolongada (IAP) fue bajo (8 %), mientras que la polifarmacia antipsicótica fue frecuente (30,6 %). El tiempo medio entre el diagnóstico de esquizofrenia y el inicio del tratamiento con clozapina fue superior a cinco años (266,47 semanas, DE: 270,4), con un promedio de 3,17 ensayos previos adecuados con antipsicóticos (DE: 1,53). Las hospitalizaciones disminuyeron significativamente después del inicio del tratamiento con clozapina (cambio medio: 1,74, DE: 1,14; tamaño del efecto grande, d = 1,09). los hallazgos obtenidos indican que la clozapina continúa siendo subutilizada en nuestro medio y resaltan la importancia de iniciarla de manera más temprana para reducir las tasas de hospitalización y mejorar los resultados clínicos.

title: [Not Available].
abstract: En las últimas décadas, el estudio del conectoma humano -mapa integral de las conexiones neuronales del cerebro- ha redefinido la comprensión del trastorno depresivo mayor (TDM) como un espectro de alteraciones funcionales y estructurales en redes cerebrales específicas. Esta revisión explora evidencia sobre patrones de conectividad funcional en el TDM, destacando la implicancia de redes como la red neuronal por defecto (RND), la red frontoparietal (RFP), la red de saliencia (RS) y los circuitos de recompensa. Se analizan patrones detectados mediante resonancia magnética funcional (RMf) y su potencial como biomarcadores para predecir respuesta a las intervenciones que hoy forman parte de las guías clínicas y constituyen el arsenal habitual en la práctica, como la psicoterapia, los antidepresivos de primera línea (ISRS), la estimulación magnética transcraneal (EMT), la terapia electroconvulsiva (TEC) y la ketamina a dosis subanestésicas. Para ello, realizamos una revisión narrativa integrativa de la literatura científica, seleccionando artículos por relevancia clínica y calidad metodológica (GRADE), incluyendo metaanálisis, revisiones sistemáticas y ensayos clínicos aleatorizados. Estos hallazgos podrían generar un cambio de paradigma hacia una psiquiatría de precisión, cada vez más centrada en la persona. Aunque persisten desafíos metodológicos que limitan su aplicación clínica, comprender el conectoma y su relación con la patogénesis del TDM es un paso fundamental hacia una verdadera atención personalizada en salud mental.

title: A Simple and Rapid Immunocytochemical Assay for Quantifying Surface Receptor Abundance in Cultured Cells.
abstract: Synaptic transmission is a fundamental process through which neurons communicate. This mechanism involves the release of neurotransmitters-such as GABA, glutamate, and norepinephrine-via exocytosis from presynaptic axon terminals. These neurotransmitters are recognized by specific receptors, including GABAR, AMPAR, and β₂AR, located on the dendritic spine membranes of postsynaptic neurons. The receptors are highly dynamic on the plasma membrane. Conventional immunocytochemical techniques label only the total expression of receptors (Simultaneously labeling all receptors on the membrane surface and within the cells) in cultured cells. Although this provides valuable information for assessing receptor abundance, it does not allow for a precise comparison of whether the number of receptors located on the cell membrane surface has changed. Here, we introduce a method for labeling plasma membrane receptors in neuronal cells using surface immunocytochemistry. By selecting antibodies that specifically recognize the extracellular domain of the receptor, receptors on the cell membrane surface can be labeled outside the intact, impermeable cell membrane.

title: Between hope and hardship: Lived experiences and quality of life among cancer patients in Kashmir.
abstract: Cancer is a leading cause of mortality worldwide and imposes significant psychosocial burdens. Beyond physical illness, patients experience psychological distress, anxiety, depression, and social isolation, particularly during active treatment. In Kashmir, cultural factors such as stigma, religious values, and gender norms strongly influence illness perception and coping; however, qualitative studies exploring lived experiences during treatment remain limited. This study aimed to explore the lived experiences, quality of life, and coping mechanisms of cancer patients in Kashmir during active treatment. A qualitative study using Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA) was conducted in July 2025 at radiation oncology department. Twenty adult inpatients with cancer were recruited purposively. In-depth, face-to-face interviews were conducted in Urdu or Kashmiri using open-ended guides. Data were audio-recorded, transcribed, translated, and analyzed following IPA principles. Researcher reflexivity and analytic memos were employed to enhance rigor. The mean age of participants was 58.15 ± 17.08 years, with breast cancer being the most common diagnosis (30%). Through an iterative and interpretative analytic process, we identified five major themes and fifteen subthemes: family as both support and a source of silence or detachment; pervasive psychological distress, including anxiety, depression, and insomnia; spirituality as a key coping mechanism; social isolation and altered interpersonal relationships; and uncertainty regarding treatment and prognosis. These findings reflect the complex interplay of familial, psychological, spiritual, and social dimensions shaping patient experiences during treatment. Cancer patients in Kashmir experience multidimensional challenges influenced by cultural and social contexts. Culturally sensitive psycho-oncology interventions that address psychological distress, family dynamics, and spiritual coping are essential to improve quality of life.

title: Scientific Frontiers and Emerging Themes in Acupuncture for Stroke: A Bibliometric Analysis.
abstract: Stroke is a leading cause of death and long-term disability worldwide, and acupuncture is widely used as a complementary therapy in stroke rehabilitation. However, the rapidly expanding and heterogeneous literature lacks systematic knowledge structure analysis and identification of emerging frontiers. This study retrieved publications related to acupuncture for stroke from the Web of Science Core Collection published from January 1, 2016, to December 31, 2025, and applied bibliometric tools including CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and Scimago Graphica to visualize publication output, collaboration networks (countries, institutions, authors), co-citation patterns, journal dual-map overlays, and keyword bursts, with the aim of delineating research hotspots and developmental trends. The results show a steady increase in annual publication output, with China, the United States, and South Korea being the most productive countries. Core research teams have been established, but cross-regional cooperation still requires strengthening. Co-citation analysis revealed classic clusters focusing on neuroplasticity, inflammatory regulation, and mechanisms of electroacupuncture. Keyword burst detection indicates that early studies centered on motor recovery and acupuncture techniques, whereas recent frontiers have shifted towards "neuroprotection", "oxidative stress", "default mode network", and "neurorehabilitation guidelines". Research hotspots are shifting from purely evaluating clinical efficacy toward multimodal mechanistic exploration and integration with evidence-based recommendations. In conclusion, the field of acupuncture for stroke is in a phase of rapid development, with the research focus shifting from basic efficacy validation to deeper mechanistic understanding and interdisciplinary integration. The knowledge maps provided in this study can help researchers quickly identify frontiers and inform future clinical trial design and guideline development.

title: Exploring rehabilitation therapists' knowledge and perspectives on the use of artificial intelligence and machine learning for persons post-stroke.
abstract: BackgroundThe integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) within the clinical work of rehabilitation therapists in post stroke rehabilitation has the potential to transform their work performance, habits, and routines. The impact could potentially enhance integration of assessment/data analysis, personalizing therapies, documentation, and promoting home program adherence.ObjectiveThis study assesses occupational and physical therapists' current perspectives on AI/ML in post-stroke clinical rehabilitation and examines perceived barriers to potential application of AI/ML in their clinical work.MethodsThis mixed methods study includes quantitative survey data collected pre/post an AI/ML educational webinar, as well as qualitative focus group analysis that includes therapist attitudes and experiences with AI/ML, practical applications to using AI/ML, as well as the difficulties associated. The recruited therapists include occupational and physical therapy practitioners from the United States and Asia. Individuals included in the study had to have a caseload of 30% persons with stroke.ResultsFour key themes emerged from qualitative analysis: 1) current clinical work practice and identified gaps, 2) current therapists' perceptions of AI/ML, 3) perceived future of AI/ML in clinical work practices and 4) steps needed for implementation. Survey data reporting frequencies of technology use and AI/ML perceptions are integrated into qualitative findings.ConclusionsTherapists can articulate potential future uses for AI/ML technology in post-stroke rehabilitation, however, remain uncertain about when, how, and at what cost utilization will be supported in clinical work environments. Therapists desire education and support to utilize the evolving technologies in practice.

title: Persistent Hypoperfusion on Post-Recanalization Digital Subtraction Angiography Perfusion Maps in Anterior Circulation Large Vessel Occlusion.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
abstract: Despite high recanalization rates with endovascular thrombectomy for large vessel occlusion stroke, a large proportion of patients remain disabled. This study aims to investigate the clinical impact of persistent hypoperfusion that was detected immediately after recanalization. In this multicenter retrospective study of patients with large vessel occlusion with near-complete or complete recanalization, perfusion maps were generated from post-recanalization digital subtraction angiography. Focal hypoperfusion within the ischemic territory was detected and categorized as regional or cortical according to spatial distribution. The primary outcome was 90-day functional independence (modified Rankin Scale 0 to 2). The associations of no-reflow and outcomes were examined by multivariable logistic regression. Among 375 patients (median age 69 [interquartile range 57-77] years; 67.5% men), persistent hypoperfusion was detected in 29.6% of patients. Patients with hypoperfusion had higher baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (median 14 versus 12, P=0.076) and more thrombectomy passes (P=0.021). The presence of persistent hypoperfusion was strongly associated with reduced functional independence (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]=0.23, 95% CI 0.13-0.39, P<0.001), higher rates of hemorrhagic transformation (aOR=1.88, 95% CI 1.14-3.11; P=0.013) and symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (aOR=2.95, 95% CI 1.20-7.23; P=0.018). Quantitative analysis revealed minimum regional cerebral blood flow as a key factor of functional outcome (aOR=1.67, 95% CI 1.07-2.60; P=0.023). There is no significant agreement with 24-hour computed tomography perfusion-defined hypoperfusion (κ=0.106, P=0.524). Persistent hypoperfusion could be detected immediately post-recanalization in one-third of successfully treated large vessel occlusion strokes. The adverse impact to functional outcome highlights its potential as an intraprocedural biomarker for future adjunctive therapies.

title: Altered Intersubject Variability of Morphological Connectivity in Cerebral Small Vessel Disease and Its Associations With Gene Expression and Cell Types.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
abstract: Cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) is a heterogeneous disorder; however, interindividual variability in morphometric brain connectivity remains unclear, as does its association with gene expression. We enrolled 65 patients with CSVD and 35 healthy controls. Individual-level morphometric brain networks were constructed from T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging, and intersubject variability of morphometric connectivity (IVMC) was quantified using a Kullback-Leibler divergence-based gray matter similarity measure. Group differences in IVMC and its associations with cognitive and clinical measures were examined. Partial least squares regression was applied to Allen Human Brain Atlas data to relate IVMC to gene expression, cell-type specificity, and biological functions. Compared with healthy controls, patients with CSVD showed globally increased IVMC (P<0.001) and significant differences across multiple functional networks (all PFalse Discovery Rate<0.05). IVMC in the sensorimotor and ventral attention networks was associated with poorer Auditory-Verbal Learning Test performance. Partial least squares regression analysis revealed that IVMC-related genes were enriched in neurodevelopmental and metabolic processes, whereas negatively weighted genes were associated with synaptic structure and glutamatergic signaling. Cell-type analyses linked IVMC alterations primarily to neuronal and glial transcriptional signatures. CSVD is associated with elevated IVMC across multiple functional networks, with changes in specific networks linked to memory impairment. These alterations may be associated with genes involved in neurodevelopment, synaptic function, and diverse neuronal and glial cell types, providing new insights into the interindividual variability of brain networks and the neurophysiological mechanisms underlying CSVD.

title: Long-COVID Associated With Incident Hypertension: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
abstract: Long COVID has been linked to persistent autonomic and vascular abnormalities, but its impact on hypertension among non-hospitalized COVID-19 convalescents remains unclear. Given the link between blood pressure and cardiovascular morbidity, understanding how long COVID modifies the risk of incident hypertension is clinically important. We conducted a longitudinal population-based study using MIRACLE-S (Multimorbidity Integrated Registry Across Care Levels in Stockholm). Adults aged 18 to 65 years without prior hypertension or hospitalization for acute COVID-19 were followed from October 2020 to January 2025. Long COVID was defined by a physician-assigned U09.9 diagnosis. The outcome was new-onset hypertension (International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision [ICD-10] I10). Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs), adjusted for age, socioeconomic status, comorbidities, mental health, and pre-pandemic health care utilization. Analyses were stratified by sex. Among 1 221 570 adults, 8365 (0.7%) were diagnosed with long COVID, and 18% developed incident hypertension during follow-up. Individuals with long COVID (women: n=5578, 16%; men: n=2787, 24%) showed an early and consistently higher cumulative incidence than unexposed individuals (P<0.0001). Long COVID was associated with increased hypertension risk overall (HR 1.14, 95% CI 1.09-1.20; P<0.001), and in women (HR 1.13, 95% CI 1.05-1.22; P=0.001) and men (HR 1.15, 95% CI 1.05-1.27; P=0.002), with stable estimates across models. Long COVID was associated with elevated risk of incident hypertension in non-hospitalized COVID-19 convalescents. These findings suggest SARS-CoV-2 infection may contribute to vascular and autonomic dysregulation affecting blood pressure, supporting structured monitoring and risk management in individuals with persistent post-COVID symptoms.

title: Prevalence and impact of cerebral small vessel lesions in mild cognitive impairment and mild dementia due to Alzheimer's disease patients in memory clinic: Preparation for anti-amyloid therapy in Thailand.
abstract: BackgroundAlzheimer's disease (AD) raises global concern with its impact on daily living. Anti-amyloid therapy (AAT) are specific treatments used in mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and mild dementia stage of AD (mild AD). Severe cerebral small vessel disease (SVD) lesions such as microbleeds, superficial siderosis, lacunes, white matter hyperintensities are listed as exclusions criteria for AAT. In Thailand, there is no prevalence study of SVD lesions specifically in these patient groups.ObjectiveThe purpose of this study is to report the prevalence of SVD burdens which are excluded in AAT, in MCI and mild AD patients in Thailand.MethodsThe study was carried out at Memory Clinic in King Chulalongkorn Memorial Hospital. Patients with amnestic MCI and mild AD were diagnosed using clinical criteria, cognitive tests and brain MRI. Visual rating scales were used to evaluate SVD burden based on STRIVE-2 criteria. Baseline characteristics and cognitive tests were retrieved from electronic medical records.ResultsThe study involving 102 patients, 73.5% had MCI, and 26.5% had mild AD. Twenty-one individuals (20.6%) had either more than 4 microbleeds, more than 2 lacunes, or Fazekas score of 3. There was no evidence of superficial siderosis. Individuals without microbleeds had a higher TMSE score (25.4 versus 23.5; p = 0.009).ConclusionsAmong patients with MCI and mild AD, 20.6% met the exclusion criteria for AAT, in part of SVD lesions. These findings provide important information for evaluating the cost-effectiveness of AAT, which become a treatment option for Thai AD patients.

title: Managing growth and puberty concerns in individuals with Duchenne muscular dystrophy: Updated guidance and future directions.
abstract: Long-term glucocorticoid therapy is standard of care for individuals with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) but often results in impaired growth and delayed or incomplete puberty, impacting their physical and psychosocial health. Although DMD endocrine care has evolved, leading to inclusion in the 2018 Care Considerations, these issues remain prevalent and concerning, and gaps in care persist. The Growth and Puberty Working Group of the OPTIMIZE DMD Consortium, an international multidisciplinary group including endocrinology and neuromuscular specialists with DMD expertise, conducted a literature review and surveyed clinicians to inform updated clinical guidance on growth and puberty. This report is based on evidence where available, plus expert consensus, and thereby provides revised guidance on the investigation and management of growth and pubertal delay, as well as hypogonadism beyond the pubertal years, among individuals with DMD. It also addresses new topics subsequent to the 2018 Care Considerations, including: 1) the dissociative glucocorticoid vamorolone and its impact on growth, and 2) gonadal function in older adolescents and young adults. With the current lack of long-term data on growth and puberty outcomes, prevailing themes underscore the importance of person- and family-centered care with informed shared decision-making aligned with individualized goals plus interdisciplinary team communication. This report also highlights specific areas in these domains in need of research. Through ongoing collaborations within the OPTIMIZE DMD Consortium, growth and puberty care continues to evolve and will inform and advance research to improve the health and quality of life of individuals with DMD.

title: Neuroprotective effects of lithium and caffeic acid co-loaded liposomes in diabetes-induced Alzheimer's disease: association with GSK-3β and β-catenin.
abstract: To investigate the therapeutic effects of co-loaded lithium (Li) and caffeic acid (CA) liposomes in diabetes-induced Alzheimer's disease rats by improving cognitive dysfunction and attenuating neurodegeneration through the modulation of β-catenin/GSK-3β signaling. Li- and CA-co-loaded liposomes were prepared by the ethanol injection method and characterized. A diabetes-induced Alzheimer's disease model was established in male Wistar rats using a high-fat diet followed by low-dose streptozotocin (35 mg/kg) administered intraperitoneally. Li- and CA-co-loaded liposomes were given via the same route every day for 4 weeks. At the end of the experiment, the animals were sacrificed, and various biochemical and oxidative stress parameters, histopathological assessments, and ELISA analyses were performed. Dual-drug-loaded Li and CA liposomal treatment significantly improved cognitive function, ameliorated metabolic dysfunction, and reduced oxidative stress by restoring antioxidant enzyme levels. Additionally, liposomes attenuated nitrite, acetylcholinesterase, and amyloid-β levels in diabetes-induced Alzheimer's rats. Histopathological assessment confirmed marked neuroprotective and pancreatic protective effects. Further, at a molecular level, Li and CA liposomal treatment reduced the expression of GSK-3β and increased the expression of β-catenin levels in rats. This study provides the first evidence demonstrating the therapeutic potential of Li- and CA-co-loaded liposomes in attenuating diabetes‑associated cognitive dysfunction.

title: Personality, dopamine, and addiction: the DRD4 Ex3 (VNTR) polymorphism and personality traits in men addicted to gambling and amphetamine.
abstract: The present study analyzed the polymorphism of the dopamine receptor gene DRD4, which is widely described in the literature as being associated with sensation seeking. Gambling disorder (GD) shares similar biological mechanisms and symptoms with substance use disorders (SUD). Therefore, a behavioral addiction group was selected for this study. During the research and recruitment process, it was revealed that all individuals undergoing treatment for gambling addiction were also addicted to amphetamine, which aligns with the biological mechanism related to brain neurotransmission. The study sample consisted of 307 male participants: 107 men diagnosed with both gambling and amphetamine addiction (study group), and 200 non-addicted men without psychiatric disorders, who served as the control group. Both groups underwent psychometric assessment using the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI) and the NEO Five-Factor Personality Inventory, and were evaluated by a board-certified psychiatrist. Genomic DNA was extracted from peripheral blood according to standard protocols. The DRD4 Ex3 polymorphism was genotyped using the PCR technique. Among individuals with gambling and amphetamine addiction who showed higher scores on the trait scale of the STAI and higher levels of Neuroticism, the s/s polymorphism of the DRD4 Ex3 gene occurred significantly more frequently compared to the control group with s/s, l/l, and s/l polymorphisms. Similarly, in addicted individuals with higher trait STAI scores and higher Neuroticism levels, the s/l polymorphism of the DRD4 Ex3 gene was significantly more prevalent than in the control group with s/s polymorphism. These findings indicate that the s/s and s/l genotypes occurred significantly more frequently in men addicted to gambling and amphetamine than in the control group, which may suggest an association between these DRD4 Ex3 variants and susceptibility to addiction. The present study demonstrates that addictions should be analyzed through a multifactorial lens. A correlation was observed between the DRD4 polymorphism and personality traits associated with addiction.

title: Testing peripheral and central therapies for provoked vestibulodynia: results from the UPDATe trial.
abstract: Vestibulodynia (VBD) is a common chronic pelvic pain condition with heterogeneous clinical presentation, including subtypes distinguished by the presence (VBD-central; VBD-c) or absence (VBD-peripheral; VBD-p) of comorbid pain conditions. Despite frequent prescribing of topical therapies such as lidocaine/estradiol and centrally-acting agents such as tricyclic antidepressants, high-quality evidence for efficacy, alone or in combination, remains limited. This study evaluated effects of peripheral, central, and combined pharmacologic treatments for two VBD subtypes and whether treatment response varied by subtype. We conducted a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 2 × 2 factorial trial (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03844412) at two academic medical centers. Women aged 18-50 with clinician-confirmed VBD were randomized to one of four treatment arms: 1) topical 5% lidocaine + 0.05% estradiol vaginal cream and placebo pill, 2) oral nortriptyline pill and placebo cream, 3) combined active pill and cream, or 4) double placebo for 16 weeks. The primary outcome was provoked vulvovaginal pain by a standardized tampon test (0-10 numeric rating scale). Of 209 participants, 69 had VBD-p and 140 had VBD-c. Tampon test pain decreased modestly across all arms, with the greatest proportion of decrease in the combined nortriptyline plus lidocaine/estradiol group, but there was no difference between subtypes. In the primary model, baseline pain strongly predicted Week 16 pain (β = 0.68, p < 0.001), and while many participants had a decrease in pain over time, no treatment produced a statistically significant reduction compared with placebo. In this trial, neither peripheral nor centrally targeted pharmacotherapies demonstrated superiority over placebo in reducing provoked vulvovaginal pain at 16 weeks.

title: RAF1 Promotes Gstt1-Mediated Ferroptosis by Promoting KDM1A Recruitment to Facilitate Pilocarpine-Induced Acute Seizure-Associated Neuronal Injury.
abstract: Seizures can cause progressive neuronal damage. Our previous studies found that RAF1 mediates vitamin D's alleviation of seizures, but the mechanism by which RAF1 acts in seizures remains unclear. The pilocarpine-induced acute seizure-associated neuronal injury (Pilo-ASNI) model and glutamate-treated HT22 cells were used. Behavioral assessments were performed to evaluate seizure severity and latency; histopathological staining was performed to examine neuronal damage and survival; and cellular assays were performed to assess cell viability, cytotoxicity, and DNA damage. Transcriptome sequencing, Co-immunoprecipitation, molecular docking, ChIP-qPCR, and ferroptosis indicators were employed to elucidate the molecular mechanism. RAF1 expression was markedly upregulated in the Pilo-ASNI model and glutamate-treated HT22 cells. RAF1 knockdown attenuated seizure severity and neuronal damage. Mechanistic studies in HT22 cells revealed that RAF1 inhibited Gstt1 transcription and promoted ferroptosis by promoting KDM1A recruitment and reducing H3K4me2 levels in the promoter region of Gstt1. Disrupting the RAF1-KDM1A interaction could inhibit ferroptosis and alleviate nerve damage, whereas Gstt1 knockdown reverses the protective effect of RAF1 inhibition. This study revealed a RAF1-driven pathway involving KDM1A-mediated epigenetic suppression of Gstt1 and subsequent ferroptosis, which may represent a potential target for neuroprotective intervention in seizures.

title: Connectivity-Guided Individualized iTBS of the Posterior Parietal Cortex in Enduring Anorexia Nervosa: Network-Level Target Engagement and Multimodal Response in a Single Case.
abstract: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is a severe, often enduring disorder with scarce biological treatments, largely unable to address its core implicit features: habit-like food restriction and body-experience disturbances. We report a single-case application of resting-state connectivity-guided intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS) to the posterior parietal cortex (PPC), a hub for body representation, peripersonal space, and affordance-based action. A 31-year-old woman with 12 years of treatment-resistant restricting AN, enrolled in an ongoing sham-controlled feasibility trial, underwent 20 active iTBS sessions to an individualized left-PPC site maximally coupled with a body-representation × affordance reference network, assessed at baseline, post-treatment, and four-month follow-up. The protocol was fully feasible and well tolerated, without significant adverse events. Clinical change was gradual, with most of the weight gain occurring after the stimulation period: BMI rose from 15.65 to 16.01 at four-month follow-up and 16.40 over subsequent clinical follow-up. Blinded global improvement was minimal; anxiety fell below threshold, whereas eating-disorder and body-shape scores remained at floor. Target-reference connectivity increased in the a priori direction, toward the healthy-control mean. Exploratory measures changed heterogeneously, only partly tracking engagement. This case supports the feasibility and mechanistic plausibility of individualized parietal targeting in enduring AN, motivating a controlled trial to test its efficacy. The parent trial is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07106645).

title: Cerebellar Network Organization in Parkinson's Disease: Functional Connectivity across Motor and Cognitive Circuits.
journal: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society
abstract: The cerebellum is increasingly recognized as a key contributor to cognitive reserve and network organization in Parkinson's disease (PD). However, the relationship of cerebello-cortical and cerebello-basal ganglia connectivity with cognitive status and nigrostriatal integrity remains incompletely understood. Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data from 172 participants with PD in the Parkinson's Precision Medicine Initiative were analyzed. Cerebello-basal ganglia and cerebello-cortical connectivity were investigated using region of interest (ROI)-to-ROI and seed-to-voxel approaches. Cerebellar connectivity was examined in relation to cognitive status, age, disease duration, motor severity, dopaminergic medication exposure, and contralateral putaminal striatal binding ratio (SBR). PD participants demonstrated robust positive cerebello-basal ganglia connectivity, particularly between lobule VI/vermis VI and the pallidum. Greater age was associated with widespread reductions in cerebello-basal ganglia coupling. Longer disease duration was associated with stronger connectivity within cerebellar and basal ganglia circuits, and among cognitively unimpaired participants, stronger lobule V connectivity with temporal regions. After adjustment for contralateral putaminal SBR, cognitively unimpaired participants generally demonstrated greater connectivity between left cerebellar regions and frontal networks, whereas cognitively impaired participants showed greater connectivity from posterior cerebellar and vermal regions, including regions implicated in cognitive processing, to temporal, parahippocampal, occipital, parietal, and somatosensory regions. Cerebellar functional connectivity in PD shows region-specific differences across cognitive status rather than uniform network loss with cognitive impairment. These findings support further investigation of cerebellar functional connectivity as a candidate biomarker of cognitive resilience and network adaptation in PD. © 2026 The Author(s). Movement Disorders published by Wiley Periodicals LLC on behalf of International Parkinson and Movement Disorder Society.

title: Reimagining UBE: Midline Biportal Endoscopic Approach with "Under the Cave" Decompression Technique for Lumbar Canal Stenosis-A Technical Note and Clinical Pearls.
abstract: The purpose of this study was to describe the technique for midline biportal endoscopic decompression (MBED) for lumbar canal stenosis by a new "under the cave" decompression technique: a paradigm shift in biportal endoscopic decompression. Laminectomy with/without fusion and facet-preserving microforaminotomy has been performed as conventional surgical treatments for lumbar canal stenosis (LCS). Recently, endoscopic spinal surgery has been introduced as a minimally invasive therapeutic modality of LCS by several authors. Here, we describe the surgical steps and technical pearls of MBED with "under the cave" decompression technique in LCS, successfully treated with a modification to the novel unilateral biportal endoscopic (UBE) spine surgery technique, that is, by using a more midline approach using primary two portals. The authors included patients who presented with chronic onset of back pain and neurogenic claudication symptoms. They were diagnosed with LCS from magnetic resonance imaging and computed tomography preoperatively. The surgery was performed via unilateral approach to achieve bilateral compression without additional skin incisions by "under the cave" decompression technique and primary two portals. This technique ensures complete decompression of the spinal canal as compared to the microscopic, tubular, and traditional UBE. Midline modification of the conventional BED done through the "under the cave" technique permits clear visualization of ipsilateral and contralateral sublaminar and foraminal areas. Owing to this enhanced exploratory capability it gives us a good outcome in terms of complete decompression of the ipsilateral and contralateral exiting roots while avoiding fusion in the elderly. The authors suggest that the new MBED, which is minimally invasive, is a good alternative treatment option for degenerative LCS.

title: Unraveling the Clinical Puzzle of Cerebral Venous Sinus Thrombosis in Ulcerative Colitis: Insights from a Systematic Review.
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) that primarily affects the colon. Among its extraintestinal complications, cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) is a rare yet potentially life-threatening emergency that can manifest as headaches, seizures, and/or neurological deficits. This review aims to characterize the clinical presentation, diagnostic modalities, and management strategies for CVST in UC patients. A comprehensive search of case reports and series yielded 1,156 studies, of which 39 met the inclusion criteria. A total of 47 patients were identified; the majority of whom were adult males (33.3%) and commonly presented with headaches (67.4%). Multi-symptom presentations were more prevalent in adults (66%; p = 0.038) and were often associated with UC flare-ups (56.4%). Patients with multiple symptoms had a higher frequency of straight and sphenoid sinus involvement compared with those with an isolated symptom ( p < 0.001). Anemia was correlated with poorer clinical outcomes ( p = 0.009). Computed tomography (CT) was the most frequently used initial imaging modality, whereas magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was more sensitive. Anticoagulation therapy with low-molecular-weight heparin and warfarin, alongside endovascular thrombectomy in select cases, was effective in improving outcomes. This review underscores the importance of early recognition, MRI-based imaging, and timely anticoagulation to improve outcomes in UC-associated CVST.

title: Thoracic Cavernous Spinal Epidural Angiolipomas (SEALs): A Three-Patient Case Report with Excellent Outcomes.
abstract: Spinal epidural angiolipomas (SEALs) are rare, benign extradural lesions accounting for 0.04 to 1.2% of all spinal axis tumors. They are typically noninfiltrating, located dorsally in the thoracic canal, and present with progressive myelopathy. Histologically, spinal epidural angiolipomas consist of mature adipose tissue interspersed with abnormal vascular channels, which may be capillary or cavernous based on vessel size. Cavernous-type spinal epidural angiolipomas are extremely rare, with only isolated reports in the literature. Surgical decompression with tumor excision is the treatment of choice in symptomatic patients, and diagnosis is confirmed on histopathological examination. We report three patients (two males, one female; age range, 28-60 years) with cavernous-type spinal epidural angiolipoma with varying presentations. MRI demonstrated dorsally located thoracic extradural lesions causing significant cord compression, and in one patient the tumor was extending into the left neural foramina. All patients underwent posterior decompression (open-door laminoplasty, or hemilaminectomy) and piecemeal gross total resection of a well-defined, noninfiltrative, highly vascular epidural mass. Histopathology in all cases confirmed a cavernous variant, composed of congested, thin-walled, dilated vessels admixed with mature adipose tissue. All patients experienced significant postoperative symptomatic improvement, without neurological deterioration or intraoperative neuromonitoring changes. Cavernous-type spinal epidural angiolipomas belong to an extremely rare subtype of spinal epidural angiolipoma that should be considered in the differential diagnosis of enhancing dorsal thoracic extradural lesions. Surgical decompression with gross-total excision offers excellent early neurological recovery in most patients, and histopathological examination remains essential for definitive diagnosis and prognostication.

title: Liposomal and Polymeric Drug Delivery of Creatine: Exploring a Multifaceted Molecule for Neurodegenerative Diseases and Beyond.
abstract: Creatine (Cr), best known as a sports supplement, is increasingly recognized for its multifaceted biological functions and broad therapeutic potential. Through its roles in cellular energy homeostasis, mitochondrial function, oxidative stress reduction, and neuroinflammation modulation, Cr has shown therapeutic potential in neurodegenerative diseases (NDs), cancer, and other disorders of energy metabolism. For NDs specifically, the application of Cr may be hindered by poor bioavailability, high dose requirements, and, most importantly, its limited ability to efficiently cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB). Advances in nanotechnology-based drug delivery systems have introduced new approaches that may help address these limitations by improving pharmacokinetics, facilitating BBB penetration, enabling targeted drug delivery, and supporting controlled drug release. Among these platforms, liposomes and polymer-based systems have been widely studied because of their favorable biocompatibility, safety profiles, and translational potential. These delivery strategies have mainly been evaluated in preclinical studies and in models of diseases other than NDs. This review examines the therapeutic potential of Cr in NDs by integrating current knowledge of its biological functions with developments in liposomal and polymeric drug delivery systems that may facilitate brain delivery and improve therapeutic outcomes. Recent studies of Cr-based formulations, Cr analogues, phosphocreatine, and other nanocarrier systems have provided insights into different approaches for improving Cr delivery and expanding its therapeutic applications. Furthermore, it summarizes recent progress in Cr-based nanomedicine, identifies current translational challenges, and highlights future research directions to advance Cr-based therapies, particularly for NDs, with potential applications in cancer and other energy metabolism-related disorders.

title: Investigating Sensorimotor Decision-Making in Depressed Individuals Using a Bayesian Approach.
abstract: Depression is among the most prevalent and disabling mental health conditions worldwide. It is associated with low mood and motivation, cognitive inefficiencies, altered reward and punishment learning, and broader executive dysfunction that can disrupt daily functioning. Depression has also been linked to differences in sensory perception, sensitivity, and processing speed. However, how depression affects sensorimotor decision-making under uncertainty remains comparatively understudied. In this study, we examined how individuals with depression process and weigh prior information relative to current sensory evidence during sensorimotor decisions. Participants completed a visuomotor coin-catching task, and behavior was analyzed within a Bayesian Decision Theory framework. We tested whether reliance on current information differed between depressed and non-depressed individuals, and whether any differences depended on uncertainty in the prior or the sensory signal. Across behavioral and computational analyses, both groups combined prior knowledge and sensory input in a qualitatively Bayesian manner, placing greater weight on current information when it was less uncertain and/or when prior information was more uncertain. The groups did not differ significantly in overall relative reliance on current information. Despite these broad similarities, more subtle differences were apparent. Model-based analyses indicated that Bayesian models outperformed heuristic alternatives in both groups, but model fit was poorer in the depressed group. Both groups adjusted sensory weighting as prior uncertainty changed, but non-depressed participants showed about twice the shift observed in depressed individuals, although this difference was not statistically significant. Together, these findings suggest that depression does not eliminate Bayesian-like integration of priors and sensory evidence, but may potentially reduce sensitivity to changes in prior reliability. Future work should test whether individual differences in symptom profiles, task demands, and cognitive flexibility moderate these effects.

title: Lifefulness - feasibility and acceptability of a self-guided digital intervention promoting mental health among older adults in Sweden.
abstract: The number and proportion of older adults (≥65 years) is increasing worldwide, already exceeding 20% in Sweden. The growing number of older adults with concurrent physical and mental health issues, pose a major challenge for healthcare, rendering a critical need for low-cost, easily accessible behavioural interventions. This single-group feasibility trial evaluated a transdiagnostic digital self-help intervention, "Lifefulness", specifically adapted for older adults and designed to promote behaviour change and mental health. Content was based on cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) and healthy ageing principles. Older adults were recruited from the community (age range 65-85) and were assigned to the six week intervention, which included three brief phone interviews focusing on program adherence. Outcomes included program use and acceptability as well as preliminary effects on quality of life and mental health outcomes. A total of 73 individuals were included. Program utility was high on average, with 72% of participants engaging with the intervention daily or several times a week. The average time spent on the three interviews was 33 min per participant. The program was associated with favourable changes in various mental health symptoms and higher ratings of quality of life and the participants reported high satisfaction and credibility. These findings support the feasibility and resource-efficiency of a digital self-help intervention for older adults. The intervention warrants further testing in a randomized trial with long-term follow-up assessments of both outcomes and healthcare consumption.

title: Risk of mortality after emergency department presentation for self-harm among children and adolescents in Wales: a population-based cohort study.
abstract: Self-harm in childhood and adolescence is associated with substantial morbidity and premature mortality, particularly from suicide. We aimed to quantify the risk of cause-specific and all-cause mortality following emergency department (ED) presentations for self-harm. In this retrospective population-based cohort study, we used anonymised, linked electronic health records from the Secure Anonymised Information Linkage (SAIL) Databank. We included children and adolescents aged 5-18 years who presented to EDs in Wales between 2008 and 2023. Individuals with at least one ED presentation for self-harm were assigned to the exposed group, and those with no recorded self-harm presentations formed the comparison group. Follow-up began at the index ED presentation and continued until death, possible emigration, or end of data availability. The primary outcome was suicide; secondary outcomes included accidental death, other causes of death, and all-cause mortality. Associations between self-harm and cause-specific mortality were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age and sex. Kaplan-Meier failure curves (1 - survival) were estimated separately for each cause of death. Between 2008 and 2023, we identified 611,336 young people who presented to EDs, of whom 14,007 (2.3%) had at least one self-harm presentation. During follow-up, 1451 deaths were recorded. Mortality was higher among those presenting with self-harm compared with controls without self-harm presentations (114 [0.8%] vs 1337 [0.2%], adjusted hazards ratio [aHR] 3.1, 95% CI 2.6-3.8). Suicide risk was markedly elevated in the first year after presentation (aHR 13.4, 95% CI 4.7-38.0) and remained increased during follow-up (aHR 4.9, 95% CI 3.4-6.9). There was a similarly increased risk of accidental death within one year (aHR 13.9, 95% CI 6.2-31.1) and after one year (aHR 5.5, 95% CI 3.9-7.7). No clear association between self-harm and other causes of death was observed. ED presentation for self-harm identifies young people at elevated risk of premature mortality. Preventive interventions should extend beyond suicide alone to address accidental deaths, particularly in the period immediately following presentation. McGill Global Health Programs Fellowship; John Fell Fund; NIHROxford Health Biomedical Research Centre; Academy of Medical Sciences; UK Department for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy.

title: The emerging role of brain-derived microparticles in trauma-induced coagulopathy after traumatic brain injury.
abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is frequently complicated by trauma-induced coagulopathy (TIC), which contributes substantially to secondary brain injury and poor clinical outcomes. The mechanisms underlying traumatic brain injury induced coagulopathy (TBI-IC) are multifactorial and involve extensive cellular alterations in endothelial cells, neutrophils, and platelets. Brain-derived microparticles (BDMPs), a subgroup of extracellular vesicles derived from brain-associated cells, attracted increasing attention due to their potential involvement in coagulation regulation after TBI. This review summarizes current evidence regarding the biological characteristics of BDMPs, their proposed contributions to coagulation abnormalities, inflammatory responses, and vascular dysfunction following TBI, as well as their potential value as biomarkers and therapeutic targets. In addition, the limitations of current evidence, including methodological heterogeneity, insufficient clinical validation, and uncertainties regarding causal mechanisms, are discussed to provide a balanced perspective on the translational potential of BDMPs in TBI-IC.

title: Angiotensin II-induced hypertension does not exacerbate α-SYNUCLEIN pathology in a mouse model of Parkinson's disease.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is characterized by progressive degeneration of nigrostriatal dopaminergic neurons accompanied by chronic neuroinflammation and α-SYNUCLEIN (α-SYN) aggregation. Increasing evidence suggests that cardiovascular comorbidities, including arterial hypertension, may contribute to neurodegenerative processes through vascular dysfunction and sustained inflammatory signaling. However, whether hypertension directly exacerbates α-SYN-induced neurodegeneration and inflammasome activation remains unclear. Here, we investigated the impact of chronic Angiotensin II (AngII)-induced hypertension in an adeno-associated viral vector (AAV)-based mouse model of PD driven by unilateral overexpression of human α-SYN in the Substantia Nigra (SN). Chronic AngII infusion produced a robust hypertensive phenotype but did not aggravate α-SYN-induced loss of tyrosine hydroxylase-positive dopaminergic neurons. Similarly, hypertension failed to modify α-SYN-driven astrogliosis, microgliosis, or microglial morphological activation. Molecular analyses revealed that α-SYN overexpression markedly increased the expression of inflammatory mediators and pyroptosis-related genes, including Nlrp3, Asc, Casp1, Il1b, Il18rap, and Gsdmd. Nevertheless, hypertension did not potentiate these responses. Immunofluorescence analyses further demonstrated that GSDMD expression was predominantly localized in IBA1-positive microglial cells and was significantly elevated following α-SYN overexpression independently of hypertensive status. Collectively, these findings indicate that chronic AngII-induced hypertension is insufficient to exacerbate early α-SYN-mediated neurodegeneration, gliosis, or inflammasome-associated pyroptotic pathways in the SN. Our study suggests that α-SYN pathology itself constitutes the dominant driver of neuroinflammatory activation in this experimental paradigm and that additional vascular or aging-related mechanisms may be required for hypertension to significantly influence PD progression.

title: The phantastic organ: predictive processing in the brain.
abstract: Neuroscience has witnessed a curious inversion over the past decades, with a switch from views of the brain as abstracting information from sensory input to a view of the brain as a constructive organ, actively generating explanations for - and sampling - the sensorium. Perhaps this inversion is not strange, but a reversion to the 'facts of perception' as laid out by Helmholtz. His enduring view of perception as inference - to the best explanation - now dominates the neurosciences in the form of the Bayesian brain paradigm and the Free Energy Principle. This review follows the story from Helmholtz's unconscious inference to modern day active inference. In particular, it uses the history of predictive coding - and how it has been generalized over the years - to furnish a framework that brings theory and empirical study in close contact, through generating mechanistic (anatomical and physiological) hypotheses about sense-making in the brain.

title: Hair cortisol concentration and basal heart rate variability differentiate long COVID from depressive disorders in youth.
abstract: Depressive symptoms are highly prevalent in long COVID (LC) and may shape its symptom burden. As hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis and autonomic nervous system (ANS) alterations have been implicated in both LC and depressive disorders, this overlap raises the question of whether both conditions share psychobiological activity patterns or show distinct profiles. The present study compared these systems between youth with LC and depressive disorders during a developmental period of heightened mental health vulnerability. Thirty-four participants were included (n = 17 per subgroup; LC: M age = 16.3 years; depressive disorders: M age = 18.8 years). Cumulative HPA axis activity was indexed via hair cortisol concentration (HCC). Basal ANS activity was assessed via 5-min resting-state heart rate variability. Fatigue, perceived stress, and psychological distress were self-reported. Group differences were analysed using Mann-Whitney U tests, with correlational analyses. Participants with depressive disorders exhibited higher HCC than those with LC (p = .004, r = .69). In contrast, participants with LC showed reduced parasympathetic activity (lower HFnu; p = .018, r = .57) and diminished autonomic adaptability (higher DFA-α1, p = .013, r = -.60). Within LC, fatigue and psychological distress were associated with attenuated parasympathetic indices, while fatigue was also linked to lower HCC. Despite overlapping symptom profiles, LC and depressive disorders showed distinct psychobiological signatures, alongside divergent autonomic and endocrine correlates of subjective symptom burden. Longitudinal mechanistic studies are needed to clarify the development and specificity of these alterations following SARS-CoV-2 infection.

title: The Advanced Therapeutics for Alzheimer's Disease Review Board: A multidisciplinary model to facilitate safe access to amyloid-targeting therapies in general neurology across the Sutter Health system.
abstract: Amyloid-targeting therapies (ATTs) require workup and monitoring that some general neurologists are uncomfortable with. Sutter Health treats over 3.5 million patients with more than 100 neurologists, but only 5 cognitive specialists. We developed the Advanced Therapeutics for Alzheimer's Disease (ATAD) Review Board, a system-wide model to address the shortage of specialists while enhancing safe access to ATTs across the health system. The ATAD Review Board comprises cognitive specialists, a neuroradiologist, a pharmacist, and a registered nurse program manager. Neurologists submit cases to the board for appropriate patient selection and re-review of cases with side effects. We reviewed 447 cases from 51 neurologists and 77% were eligible for treatment. The annual volume increased 148% in 2025. Total amyloid-related imaging abnormality rate was 17.4% for lecanemab and 28.8% for donanemab. We describe a system-wide review board model that supported ATT prescribing by general neurologists and expanded safe access to ATTs across a large integrated health system.

title: Imaging Neuroscience: The First Three Years-Editorial.
abstract: In April 2023, the editors of NeuroImage and NeuroImage:Reports resigned, and a month later launched Imaging Neuroscience. NeuroImage had been the leading journal in our field, but its publication fee had reached a level that many considered unethical and unsustainable. We therefore launched Imaging Neuroscience with MIT Press, with the goal of replacing NeuroImage as our field's leading journal, and with greater control by the academic community over publication fees and adoption of modern and ethical publishing practices. Three-and-a-half years later, as I step down as Editor-in-Chief, this editorial gives a brief summary of how things are going. The bottom line is: very well indeed!

title: Aerobic exercise, whey protein, and creatine in adolescents: implications for performance, recovery, immunometabolic adaptation, and muscle-bone-brain crosstalk.
abstract: Adolescence constitutes a pivotal developmental phase for the enhancement of musculoskeletal and metabolic wellbeing, as well as neurodevelopment, during which specific exercise regimens and nutritional interventions can precipitate enduring physiological transformations. Although aerobic exercise has conventionally been linked to enhancements in cardiovascular fitness and metabolic control, the confluence of this form of exercise with anabolic and ergogenic supplements, including whey protein and creatine, in adolescent populations has not been extensively investigated. This narrative review examines current evidence on aerobic exercise, whey protein, and creatine in adolescents, with particular emphasis on exercise performance, recovery, immunometabolic adaptation, and muscle-bone-brain crosstalk. A narrative literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar using combinations of terms related to aerobic exercise, whey protein, creatine, adolescents, exercise performance, recovery, immunometabolism, and muscle-bone-brain signaling. Relevant peer-reviewed studies published from database inception to May 2026 were considered, with emphasis on adolescent human studies and selected mechanistic evidence from experimental and adult populations when directly relevant to biological interpretation. Aerobic exercise promotes oxidative metabolic processes, mitochondrial functionality, and endurance performance, thereby enhancing mitochondrial biogenesis and metabolic flexibility. Whey protein supplies critical amino acids that incite muscle protein turnover and modulate pivotal signaling cascades, thereby supporting muscle remodeling and recovery. Creatine, in addition to its function in the swift regeneration of adenosine triphosphate, plays a significant role in cellular hydration, the preservation of mitochondrial integrity, and the maintenance of antioxidant defense mechanisms, while also potentially influencing brain energy metabolism and brain-derived neurotrophic factor-mediated neuroplasticity. Emerging evidence further suggests that exercise and nutritional interventions may influence inflammatory mediators, myokines, osteokines, and neurotrophic pathways involved in muscle-bone-brain communication. However, mechanistic evidence is frequently derived from animal or non-adolescent human studies, and direct evidence for combined interventions in adolescents remains limited. Overall, aerobic exercise, whey protein, and creatine may have complementary roles in supporting exercise performance, recovery, and metabolic adaptation during adolescence, although further well-controlled adolescent studies are needed to establish their long-term efficacy, safety, and optimal use.

title: Establishing a transdiagnostic dimension of early childhood depressive symptoms using the Preschool Feelings Checklist-Scale.
abstract: Young child depressive symptoms are associated with various concurrent and future psychiatric problems, indicating early transdiagnostic risk for psychopathology. We now need studies that identify and test the robustness, reliability, and validity of early emerging depressive symptom dimensions, examining them relative to wide-ranging forms of psychopathology. Psychometric methods are suitable for such investigations. In a sample of 547 young children (ages 3-7 years) enriched for internalizing problems, preregistered analyses on the psychometric properties of the Preschool Feelings Checklist-Scale (PFC-S) investigated the robustness and interpretation of young child depressive symptom dimensions using exploratory structural equation models (ESEMs) and correlations alongside related constructs. We also tested the accuracy with which the PFC-S distinguished children based on broadband psychiatric diagnostic profiles and clinical concern. A bifactor ESEM with three group factors (Social and Behavioral Anhedonia, Emotional and Behavioral Dysregulation, and Excessive Guilt and Sadness) and residual correlations accounting for item wording similarities was the most valid PFC-S model (comparative fit index/Tucker-Lewis index = 0.98; root mean squared error of approximation = 0.06; standardized root mean squared residual = 0.03). Only the general factor emerged as reliable (ω H = 0.91; H = 0.96; factor determinacy = 0.99).
