title: Ganoderma lucidum polysaccharides alleviate cognitive impairment in sleep-deprived mice: Association with gut microbiota remodeling.
abstract: Sleep deprivation (SD) can impair cognitive function through multiple processes, including systemic inflammation, oxidative stress, and synaptic dysfunction, yet effective interventions remain limited. Therefore, this study investigated whether Ganoderma lucidum polysaccharides (GLP) could alleviate SD-induced cognitive impairment and whether such effects were accompanied by changes in gut microbiota, fecal metabolism, and indicators related to the microbiota-gut-brain (MGB) axis. In a chronic SD mouse model, GLP administration not only improved memory performance and anxiety-like behaviors but also increased hippocampal BDNF levels and the expression of the synapse proteins PSD-95 and SYP. Integrated 16S rRNA sequencing and untargeted metabolomics revealed that GLP remodeled the gut microbial landscape, enriching genera such as Kurthia and Roseburia, suppressing Escherichia-Shigella, and shifting fecal metabolic profiles, with elevated gamma-glutamylglycine and reduced cyclic melatonin as representative metabolic signatures. These peripheral changes were accompanied by reduced serum lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and inflammatory cytokines, alongside a more favorable hippocampal profile characterized by enhanced Nrf2-related antioxidant responses, improved AQP4 distribution, and diminished Aβ1-42 deposition. Correlation analyses further linked taxa responsive to GLP, particularly Kurthia and Escherichia-Shigella, to metabolite shifts, behavioral outcomes, and hippocampal markers. Collectively, these findings indicate that the cognitive benefits of GLP in SD mice are closely associated with coordinated changes across the MGB axis, providing a foundation for further exploration of GLP as a functional food candidate.

title: Impact of glyphosate management techniques on residue levels and chemical composition of Coffea arabica and Coffea canephora beans.
abstract: Glyphosate is the most extensively applied herbicide and can be absorbed by non-target plants potentially altering their chemical profile. Coffee, the second most consumed beverage worldwide, relies on glyphosate use to sustain productivity. However, limited evidence exists regarding absorption of soil-applied glyphosate, its possible translocation into coffee beans, and chemical changes. This study investigated the impact of different glyphosate application techniques on chemical composition and residue accumulation in Coffea arabica and Coffea canephora beans. Plants were subjected to seven treatments varying in spray nozzle types (flat-fan and cone) and application schedules (October and December; October and February; and October, December and February). Glyphosate residues were quantified by LC-MS/MS, while gravimetric analyses assessed moisture, ash, and soluble extract yield; chlorogenic acids and caffeine were determined by UHPLC-PDA. Results demonstrated that glyphosate is absorbed and translocated to beans, with residue levels ranging from 0.0 to 0.5 mg/kg. Nonetheless, applications performed in October and December resulted in lower residues levels compared to schedules performed until February, with no significant alterations related to the negative control. Contrary to expectations, chlorogenic acids levels were not affected by glyphosate application. Similarly, despite isolated differences, none of the evaluated parameters were significantly influenced by glyphosate use. These findings were supported by PCA and PERMANOVA, which revealed that sample discrimination was influenced exclusively by species and crop year. Further studies investigating additional coffee bean compounds, particularly from a food safety perspective, are needed to provide a more comprehensive understanding of the effects of glyphosate on coffee beans.

title: Comprehensive chemical and multivariate characterization of Amazonian guarana (Paullinia cupana) seed coats: Insights for sustainable valorization.
abstract: Guarana is a fruit native to the Amazon and is widely recognized for its stimulant properties and economic importance in Brazil, the world's leading producer. However, guarana processing utilizes only the seeds, generating substantial amounts of residues, particularly seed coats. Despite being treated as waste, these residues may constitute valuable sources of nutrients and bioactive compounds, offering opportunities for upcycling and sustainable valorization. This study comprehensively characterized guarana seed coats (PR1, PR2, and PR3) sourced from producers in Amazonas State, Brazil, through integrated physicochemical, compositional, chromatographic, and multivariate analyses. The samples evaluated exhibited high dietary fiber (61.96-64.42%) and protein contents (15.93-17.33%), alongside relevant concentrations of structural carbohydrates (total lignin: 27.59-39.98%; cellulose: 17.19-31.52%; hemicellulose: 9.45-26.27%) and essential minerals, particularly Ca, Mg, K, Cu, and Mn. The residues also showed high concentrations of bioactive compounds, mainly caffeine (16.96-28.88 mg/g) and epicatechin (0.50-12.53 mg/g). Multivariate analyses (PCA and ComDim) revealed distinct compositional profiles among the evaluated production sources, with PR1 as being associated with the highest levels of bioactive compounds, PR2 with elevated structural carbohydrate contents, and PR3 with higher concentrations of essential minerals. Overall, the findings provide a comprehensive compositional basis to support the sustainable valorization of guarana seed coats and future studies evaluating their technological functionality, safety, and food applications, contributing to circular economy strategies.

title: Human febrile illness associated with Yanggou tick virus: Clinical characteristics and epidemiological links to rodents.
abstract: We identified Yanggou tick virus (YGTV), a segmented flavivirus previously unrecognized as a human pathogen, in a patient presenting with fever and headache. This study aims to characterize the epidemiology and clinical manifestations of YGTV infection in patients with fever of unknown origin (FUO). We conducted a surveillance study at the First Hospital of Jilin University (2020-2025) involving 1,011 patients with FUO. Concurrently, ticks and rodents in the vicinity of the patients' residences and workplaces were collected for viral detection. YGTV infection was confirmed via PCR assays. Positive samples were used for viral isolation, genome amplification, and phylogenetic characterization. An Apodemus agrarius challenge model was established to evaluate viral persistence and shedding. Of the 30 confirmed cases of YGTV infection, 10 were co-diagnosed with hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS). The patients showed no clear seasonality or geographic bias. Notably, rodent contact (43.3%) was a more frequent risk factor than tick bites (6.7%). While clinical presentations were non-specific, nearly 50% of the patients presented with gastrointestinal and neurological symptoms. YGTV was isolated from patients, ticks, and A. agrarius (the latter often co-infected with Hantaan virus). Animal models confirmed persistent splenic infection and viral shedding via oral and fecal routes. Our findings establish YGTV as an underdiagnosed cause of human febrile illness, underscoring the transmission risks posed by tick vectors and rodent reservoirs. These results highlight the urgent need for enhanced clinical surveillance and diagnostic screening among patients presenting with FUO, particularly in regions where the virus is endemic.

title: The regulatory roles of the medial septum and hippocampus in spatial memory impairment of PTSD mice.
abstract: This experiment was based on the establishment of an analogue of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in mice, aiming to explore the regulatory effects of the medial septum (MS) and the hippocampus (HIP) on spatial memory impairment in mice, and to establish a theoretical foundation for revealing the pathological basis of PTSD-related spatial memory impairment. The PTSD mouse model was prepared, behavioral testing, FluoroGold (FG) retrograde tracing technique, viral tracing technique, in vivo fiber photometry recording technique, chemogenetic technology and in vivo electrophysiological recording techniques were applied to observe and analyze the changes in spatial memory ability and the central regulatory mechanism. PTSD mice showed heightened anxiety, impaired spatial memory, suppressed Sch-CA1 long-term potentiation, and hyperactivity of MS-CA1 cholinergic neurons; chemogenetic inhibition of this pathway rescued both the behavioral and synaptic plasticity deficits. The regulation of spatial memory impairment in PTSD mice involves MS-resident cholinergic neurons. We found a cholinergic pathway connection between MS and CA1, and this pathway may regulate murine spatial cognition by influencing the synaptic plasticity of Sch-CA1.

title: Using data-driven, lesion-symptom mapping to study the relationship between neural and theoretical components of numeracy.
abstract: Numeracy, the ability to understand and manipulate numbers, is a crucial foundational ability for many daily life skills. Numeracy tasks have been categorized using different taxonomic approaches, and understanding of the relationship between tasks categories and neural models of numeracy remains poor. In this study, we use the lesion method to address this key gap. The study employs a data-driven approach with support vector regression lesion-symptom mapping (SVR-LSM) of extracted factors from two left hemisphere chronic stroke survivor datasets: one with data from a battery of math and language tests (N = 100) and the other with data from the EC301 math battery (N = 64). We find that our data best support a separation of number tasks requiring verbal vs. magnitude number knowledge, aligning with a broad theme that emerges across theories in different variations. This is supported by distinct neuroanatomical correlates that link verbal coding of number to the language-centered regions including left perisylvian area and insula, and that link magnitude coding to the parietal lobe, as described in prior models. Our findings indicate that these two different sources of representation variously contribute to a range of math tasks, including different types of arithmetic calculation tasks, in ways which cannot be cleanly defined by one singular theoretical model of math cognition.

title: Redox-responsive peptide assemblies for precision theranostic.
abstract: Redox biology represents a universal molecular language that encodes biochemical gradients, distinguishing healthy from diseased tissues with significant precision. The convergence of redox signaling and peptide self-assembly results in a versatile chemical framework for next-generation theranostics. Peptides, programmable, biocompatible, and hierarchically organized, can translate subtle oxidative cues into structural transitions, functional activation, and real-time diagnostic output. Redox-responsive molecular assemblies leveraging disulfide exchange, thiol oxidation, methionine sulfoxidation, and dithiane chemistry enable dynamic assembly, phase transition, or disintegration based on local redox potential. Redox dysregulation, encompassing reactive oxygen species and reactive nitrogen species imbalance, glutathione depletion, and iron-driven lipid peroxidation - governs diverse pathologies from cancer to neurodegeneration. In parallel, beyond traditional delivery platforms, redox-activated phase-separating peptides forming coacervate microdroplets have emerged as versatile drug vectors with high-capacity recruitment of nucleic acids, proteins, and small molecules, with cytosolic release triggered by glutathione. These condensate-like materials exhibit rapid and very high encapsulation efficiency, intracellular uptake, and redox-coded responsiveness. Additionally, imaging probes coupling redox-triggered bond cleavage with optical or magnetic signal activation allow real-time visualization of redox landscapes during therapy. From a translational perspective, progress is accelerated by advances in large-scale solid-phase peptide synthesis, redox-stable manufacturing workflows, and evolving regulatory frameworks. Future redox-responsive peptide coacervates are envisioned as programmable "chemical processors" that sense oxidative flux, interpret biochemical input, and deliver microenvironments-specific outputs. Such adaptive, information-rich architectures position peptide-based redox nanotheranostics as an emerging class of biomaterials capable of combining therapeutic action with the dynamic redox logic of diseases.

title: Waterless versus soap-and-water perineal hygiene in fully dependent hospitalized patients: a multicenter randomized trial.
abstract: This study evaluated the microbiological effectiveness and organizational impact of waterless perineal hygiene compared with traditional soap-and-water cleansing in fully dependent hospitalized patients, addressing a gap in evidence within acute care settings. This multicenter, randomized, open-label superiority trial was conducted in 10 medical and geriatric wards across four hospitals in Northern Italy. Fully dependent adult inpatients were randomized 1:1 to waterless hygiene or standard soap-and-water care. The primary outcome was the proportion of participants achieving a ≥90% reduction in microbial load between pre- and post-procedure perineal swabs. Secondary outcomes included procedure duration, patient and healthcare professional satisfaction, and agreement between evaluations. A total of 468 participants were analyzed (239 control; 229 experimental). The experimental procedure achieved a higher proportion of ≥90% microbial reduction compared with standard care (47.2% vs 37.2%; p=0.030), corresponding to an absolute risk difference of 9.9% (95% CI 1.0-18.8) and a risk ratio of 1.27 (95% CI 1.02-1.57). Procedure duration was similar between groups (median 10 vs 11 minutes; p=0.311). Satisfaction was high in both groups, with more favorable perceptions of fragrance and overall hygiene in the experimental group. Waterless perineal hygiene demonstrated greater immediate microbiological cleansing effectiveness than standard soap-and-water hygiene without increasing procedure time. Further studies are needed to determine whether these microbiological findings translate into improved clinical outcomes, including healthcare-associated infections.

title: A GLP-1/apelin dual receptor agonist shows neuroprotective effects in the MPTP mouse model of Parkinson's disease.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a chronic disorder with no disease-modifying treatment available. The glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) class of drugs is on the market to treat diabetes and obesity. GLP-1 drugs have also shown neuroprotective effects in animal models and clinical trials in PD patients. Apelin (APJ) is an adipokine peptide hormone with neuroprotective actions in preclinical studies. Here, we test the effects of a rationally designed bifunctional peptide, namely ELA (exendin-4-linker-apelin), in the MPTP mouse model of PD. The single GLP-1 receptor agonist liraglutide was used as a comparator. Motor activity was improved by both drugs (open field, pole test, Rotarod), and the inflammation response was reduced (activation of microglia and astrocytes, pro-inflammatory cytokine levels). In addition, synapse numbers were improved in the striatum (Golgi strain, TEM), expression of synapse-associated proteins was enhanced, alongside reduced expression of genes that increase mitochondrial fission. Mitochondrial fusion gene expressions (Opa1, Mfn2, Drp1) and mitochondrial morphology were also normalized (TEM). ELA was superior to liraglutide in some, but not all, parameters measured. The results suggest that the rational design of bifunctional peptides targeting both GLP-1 and APJ pathways-with optimized pharmacokinetics and enhanced blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability-merits further investigation as a strategy for developing more effective treatments for PD.

title: Beyond the brain-centric view: A systems physiology framework for exercise-induced neuroprotection in Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is regarded as a multifactorial disease that combines central pathological changes and peripheral organ dysfunction. Its core features include Aβ protein deposition, tau protein pathology, synaptic dysfunction, and neuroinflammation. Exercise has been proven to be one of the most effective non-pharmacological intervention measures. However, its mechanism of action in AD has not been fully elucidated from the traditional brain-centered research perspective. Moreover, most existing studies focus on isolated organ systems or a single signaling pathway, failing to fully reflect the overall peripheral-cerebral physiological interaction mechanism required for neuroprotective effects of exercise. This article provides a structured narrative synthesis of current evidence regarding how exercise may influence AD-related pathological processes through multiple peripheral organ systems. It clarifies the communication mechanisms between these systems and the central nervous system through endocrine, immune, metabolic, neural, and vascular pathways. The study shows that exercise functions by coordinating the regulation of peripheral physiological functions, rather than relying on a single target mechanism. Exercise can regulate multiple signaling pathways such as muscle-brain, gut-brain, liver-brain, adipose-brain, bone-brain, and immune-brain, improving overall metabolic flexibility, inflammation regulation, vascular function, and neuroimmune homeostasis; these peripheral adaptive changes further act on the central nervous system, regulating blood-brain barrier(BBB) integrity, microglial cell activity, neuronal energy metabolism, neurovascular coupling, and synaptic plasticity. In summary, the neuroprotective effect induced by exercise stems from the integration of multiple systems' physiology, rather than isolated molecular signal transduction. This review synthesizes current evidence on exercise-induced peripheral-central interactions in AD from a systems physiology perspective, highlighting the significance of integrating peripheral biomarkers, multi-organ interactions, and central outcomes. It provides a theoretical framework for future personalized and mechanism-oriented exercise intervention studies.

title: Partial convergence of alternative polyadenylation changes across ALS-Associated RNA-Binding proteins.
abstract: Alternative polyadenylation (APA) regulates transcript 3'-end architecture, stability, localization, and translation. Although RNA-binding protein dysfunction is central to amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), whether different ALS-associated proteins cause shared APA abnormalities remains unclear. We analyzed poly(A)-site usage after TDP-43 knockdown, TDP-43 K263E expression, FUS knockout, FUS P525L expression, and MATR3 knockout. Using false-discovery rate (FDR) < 0.05 as the primary criterion, evidence varied markedly among datasets. FUS knockout produced the strongest response, with 373 significant events affecting 239 genes. Three events involving two genes remained significant after TDP-43 knockdown, and two events involving one gene remained significant in the TDP-43 K263E dataset. No events survived FDR correction after FUS P525L expression or MATR3 knockout, and no FDR-significant events or genes were shared between datasets. We therefore examined nominal events (unadjusted P < 0.05) as an explicitly exploratory layer. Nominal event overlap was enriched in 7 of 10 pairwise comparisons, and nominal gene overlap in 9 of 10. TDP-43 knockdown and TDP-43 K263E showed the strongest directional agreement: 65 nominal events were shared; 25 were directionally classified in both datasets, of which 23 were concordant. FUS knockout and FUS P525L also showed enriched nominal overlap, but without significant directional concordance or correlated ΔPAU responses. Thus, FUS loss induces a robust FDR-supported APA phenotype, whereas evidence is substantially weaker in other contexts. Cross-dataset similarities occur mainly among exploratory nominal targets and do not consistently extend to direction or magnitude. APA responses therefore show partial, context-dependent convergence rather than a universal defect.

title: Synchronized audiovisual stimulation enhances neural entrainment: convergent evidence from complementary EEG biomarkers.
abstract: Rhythmic sensory stimulation modulates oscillations via frequency-specific entrainment, but synchronized auditory contributions remain unclear, and periodic-aperiodic decomposition has not been applied to audiovisual entrainment. Forty adults received visual stimulation at 8, 20, and 40 Hz, alone (VF) or synchronized with binaural beats of identical frequencies (VF + BB). EEG was analyzed using power spectral density (PSD), topographical mapping, Sample Entropy (SampEn), Lempel-Ziv Complexity (LZC), Phase-Locking Regularity (PLR), and IRASA to separate periodic (SSVEP) from aperiodic (1/f) contributions. Visual flicker induced frequency-specific entrainment, and binaural beats modulated responses frequency-dependently. At 8 Hz, flicker elicited a periodic SSVEP; adding binaural beats enhanced this component and increased aperiodic activity. At 20 Hz, synchronized audiovisual stimulation enhanced both periodic and aperiodic components. At 40 Hz, IRASA showed no significant periodic modulation; VF + BB produced a widespread increase in aperiodic offset and exponent, absent under VF alone. VF + BB reduced SampEn across all frequencies and increased PLR at 8 and 20 Hz, whereas LZC decreased at 8 Hz and increased at 20 Hz. Synchronized audiovisual stimulation produced frequency-dependent changes in EEG spectral organization. At 8 and 20 Hz, adding binaural beats enhanced the periodic SSVEP component, with changes in the aperiodic background. At 40 Hz, conventional PSD showed increased gamma activity, but periodic-aperiodic decomposition did not reveal significant periodic enhancement; audiovisual stimulation primarily altered aperiodic offset and exponent. Complementary regularity and phase-based measures showed frequency-dependent temporal changes. Findings highlight combining conventional spectral analysis, periodic-aperiodic decomposition, and complementary EEG biomarkers to characterize synchronized audiovisual stimulation.

title: Neuronal activity-regulated histone demethylase KDM7A controls hippocampal gene expression and behavior.
abstract: The role of lysine demethylase 7A (KDM7A) in the mammalian brain remains largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate that KDM7A occupies thousands of genomic loci in hippocampal chromatin and that both its expression and chromatin binding are dynamically regulated by neuronal activity in culture and in vivo. To define its functional relevance, we generated mouse models with either complete loss of KDM7A or disrupted enzymatic activity and assessed neurological phenotypes. Integrating cellular and molecular analyses with transcriptomic and chromatin-occupancy profiling and behavioral assessments, we show that KDM7A is required for the proper transcriptional regulation of genes implicated in neuronal physiology and synaptic plasticity. In line with these transcriptional alterations, KDM7A-deficient mice display hyperlocomotion, reduced anxiety-like behavior, decreased sensitivity to pro-epileptic agents, and task-dependent changes in cognitive performance. Together, our findings identify KDM7A as a key epigenetic regulator of neuronal gene expression and behavior in the mammalian brain.

title: Radiosurgical capsulotomy for treatment-resistant obsessive-compulsive disorder through a network neuroscience lens.
abstract: Severe, treatment-resistant obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) remains disabling despite optimized pharmacotherapy and exposure and response prevention (ERP). Radiosurgical capsulotomy is an irreversible ablative intervention reserved for highly selected patients. This narrative review examines evidence from structural MRI, diffusion imaging, functional connectivity, electrophysiology, and radiobiology. The search was supplemented by a reproducible PubMed search across eight prespecified modules (856 records before and 739 after deduplication), with an audited 102-record core SRS/OCD set. Structural lesion mapping and a small longitudinal diffusion study support investigating pathway involvement alongside lesion volume, but do not establish a validated network mechanism or individualized targeting biomarker. Functional MRI and EEG findings in OCD and connectivity studies of other interventions provide complementary evidence but require cautious cross-modality extrapolation. Single-session irradiation must be distinguished from thermal capsulotomy; dose, prescription isodose, irradiated volume, and delayed toxicity require joint interpretation. We use "functional disconnection" as a hypothesis concerning downstream effects of tissue injury, not evidence of a nonablative or reversible treatment. Priorities include harmonized longitudinal imaging, dose-volume-connectivity analyses, cognitive and behavioral surveillance, and controlled evaluation of ERP timing. Current evidence supports a network-informed research framework without establishing a post-radiosurgery plasticity window or superiority of connectivity over conventional planning variables.

title: Real-life efficacy and tolerance of trametinib in BRAF-rearranged low-grade gliomas: A multicenter study.
abstract: MEK inhibition has demonstrated activity in pediatric low-grade gliomas (pLGGs) driven by BRAF rearrangements, but data on trametinib remain limited, regarding efficacy, short and long-term toxicities. We conducted a retrospective multicenter study of patients with BRAF-rearranged non NF1 pLGGs receiving trametinib across three French pediatric oncology centers. Plasma concentrations were monitored. Between 2015 and 2023, 46 patients had a median age of 8.7 years (range 1.2-18.6). Trametinib achieved a radiological disease control rate of 78% (36/46), including 65% partial or minor responses and 13% stable disease, with activity even in heavily pretreated (up to 6 lines) and chemotherapy-refractory tumors. Clinical improvement occurred in 72% of patients. Median treatment duration was 14.2 months (range, 1.0-55.1). Among 35 patients who discontinued treatment, 37% remained treatment-free after a median follow-up of 16.1 months (4.3-44.2). Grade 3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in one-third of patients. Common toxicities included cutaneous events (69%), paronychia (64%), gastrointestinal symptoms (51%), elevated creatine kinase (54%) and transaminases (31%). Ophthalmologic (16%) toxicities and epistaxis (17%) of which 35% were grade 2 and required intervention, were observed. Body mass index Z-score increased during treatment but was clinically significant (≥1 SD) and related to trametinib in only 17% of patients. Pharmacokinetics showed high interpatient variability, with no correlation between plasma concentrations and efficacy or toxicity. Trametinib demonstrates sustained activity in BRAF-rearranged pLGGs, including in heavily pretreated patients. This study represents the largest reported cohort of BRAF-rearranged pLGGs, expanding prior evidence and supporting a class effect of MEK inhibitors.

title: Thalamocortical connectivity associated with fatigue after accounting for depressive symptoms in stroke survivors and controls.
abstract: Post-stroke fatigue is common and disabling, yet rarely distinguished from co-occurring depression, limiting understanding of its neural substrates. We examined resting-state fMRI correlates of post-stroke fatigue while accounting for depressive symptoms. We studied 103 stroke patients and 29 age-matched controls from a longitudinal neuroimaging cohort. Fatigue was assessed via the SF-36 Vitality subscale and depression via the Geriatric Depression Scale - Short (GDS-15). Linear mixed-effects models evaluated associations between vitality and resting-state functional connectivity, adjusting for depression and covariates. Residualized vitality models served as sensitivity analyses to isolate fatigue variance independent of depressive symptoms, with FDR correction applied within feature families. In depression-adjusted models, higher vitality (lower fatigue) was associated with increased frontoparietal-limbic connectivity (β = 0.0013, FDR q = 0.048), though this did not survive depression residualization. In a residualized sensitivity analysis, higher vitality (lower fatigue) was associated with reduced thalamus-insula and thalamus-ventral attention network connectivity (thalamus-insula: β = -0.0071, FDR q = 0.011; thalamus-VAN: β = -0.0043, FDR q = 0.012); these associations were attenuated and did not survive correction in the primary depression-adjusted model (q ≈ 0.075). Fatigue was associated with both frontoparietal-limbic and thalamocortical connectivity, although the thalamic associations were attenuated after adjustment for depressive symptoms in the primary analysis and were most evident in residualized sensitivity analyses. These findings suggest that fatigue and depressive symptoms may involve both shared and potentially distinct neural correlates. Point estimates were smaller in stroke participants than controls, providing no evidence that the observed associations were stroke-specific. Future work should determine whether these relationships are unique to stroke or reflect broader neural correlates of fatigue across clinical populations.

title: Strategies and barriers in radiation risk communication in medical imaging: A scoping review of radiographers' practices.
abstract: Radiation risk communication allows patients to make an informed decision, enhancing their autonomy during diagnostic imaging procedures. It can also reduce anxiety and improve patient cooperation. However, evidence suggests that radiographers often provide inadequate or unclear information about radiation risks. Several barriers further limit effective communication, thereby undermining patient awareness, informed decision-making, and overall patient-centred care. This study explored strategies and barriers in radiation risk communication. A scoping review was conducted using Arksey and O'Malley's framework and reported in line with PRISMA-ScR. Literature searches were performed in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science. Included studies focused on professional guidelines and empirical evidence on radiation risk communication. Thematic analysis identified three key themes: (i) radiation risk communication approaches, (ii) barriers to effective communication, and (iii) needs for development in communication practice. Radiographers predominantly used active or passive verbal communication approaches when discussing radiation risks. Key barriers included fear of causing patient anxiety, limited knowledge and low confidence in risk communication, ambiguity in role responsibility, and lack of appropriate resources. Recommended areas for improvement included enhanced radiographer education and training, use of interactive communication strategies, and incorporation of supportive materials such as posters and patient information leaflets. Radiation risk communication practices among radiographers remain inconsistent and often inadequate despite their central role in patient education and informed consent. Standardised protocols and institutional support are required to improve consistency, clarity, and effectiveness of communication in clinical practice. Strengthening education and training in radiation risk communication, clarifying professional roles, and implementing structured communication protocols alongside supportive patient education materials can improve patient understanding, enhance informed consent, and strengthen trust while promoting safer, patient-centred care.

title: Real-world effectiveness and safety of Ocrelizumab in a gulf multiple sclerosis cohort: extension of the Q-OCRE study to 451 patients.
abstract: Real-world evidence on ocrelizumab in multiple sclerosis (MS) from the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) is limited. We extended our original Q-OCRE cohort (n = 60) to evaluate effectiveness and safety in an ethnically diverse Gulf population. In a single-center retrospective cohort of all patients starting ocrelizumab at Hamad General Hospital, Doha, Qatar (October 2017-May 2025), the primary outcome was No Evidence of Disease Activity (NEDA-3) at Year 1; secondary outcomes were annualized relapse rate (ARR), Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) trajectory, 24-week confirmed disability worsening (CDW), persistence, and safety. A total of 451 patients were included (86.7% RRMS, 7.1% SPMS, 6.2% PPMS; 57.6% female; mean age 34.3 years; median follow-up 18.1 months; 696 person-years). The cohort was mildly affected at initiation (median EDSS 1.0; 42% with no relapse in the prior 2 years). ARR fell from 0.381 to 0.046, an 87% reduction (IRR 0.13, 95% CI 0.07-0.22, p < 0.001), preserved in patients meeting trial-like activity criteria (IRR 0.09). The EDSS slope was -0.04 points/year (p = 0.03) with a phenotype-by-time interaction (p < 0.001): RRMS improved while progressive forms worsened. NEDA-3 was 59.0% at Year 1 and 61.7% at Year 2. 24-week CDW reached 8.9% at 36 months, progressive phenotype being the only independent predictor (HR 5.02). Persistence was 90.7% at 36 months. Infusion-related reactions occurred in 18.4%, adjudicated opportunistic infections in 1.0%, IgG below 7 g/L in 6.9%, and incident malignancy in 0.4%, with no deaths and no progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy. Ocrelizumab showed robust effectiveness and a favorable safety profile in this Gulf cohort, with disability trajectories dissociating by phenotype.

title: Multiple sclerosis occurrence with gut microbial metabolites and sex hormones.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic immune and neurodegenerative condition that affects the central nervous system (CNS). Multiple factors, both genetic (including the HLA gene locus) and environmental (Epstein-Barr virus, low vitamin D levels), may contribute to MS development. Growing evidence supports the importance of the gut-brain axis and hormones in disease pathogenesis and progression. This review focuses on identifying the role of specific gut microbial products (short-chain fatty acids, tryptophan derivatives, bile acids, and polyamines) in this process and how they affect the immune system, blood-brain barrier (BBB), and glial cells. The review will also describe key differences between female and male patients with MS, including the higher prevalence in females and the tendency toward a progressive course in males. Estrogens, progesterone, and androgens have immunomodulatory, neuroprotective, and remyelinating activities, and this review will describe their impact on multiple sclerosis based on preclinical and clinical findings from pregnancy, menopause, and hormone replacement therapy. This paper discusses the intersection of these ideas through the "microgenderome" concept, which describes how hormones influence gut microbiota composition and how the microbiota, in turn, modulates hormone metabolism and levels.

title: Sex differences in neuropsychiatric genetics: progress in understanding mechanisms of risk and protection.
abstract: Sex differences in the prevalence and clinical presentation of neuropsychiatric disorders suggest a corresponding divergence in underlying biological risk mechanisms between males and females. Advances in neuropsychiatric genetics have started to resolve these differences, defining sex-differential genetic architectures and risk loci across common and rare variants on the autosomes and sex chromosomes, with the study of major depressive disorder and neurodevelopmental disorders leading the way. As we look to translate sex-differential genetic signals into mechanistic understanding, emerging evidence highlights roles for sex chromosome dosage and gonadal hormone signaling. Sex-aware functional genomics approaches further provide genome-scale information for aligning genetic risk with these sex-differential biological drivers, baseline sex differences, and sex-differential disorder states. Moving forward, continued progress toward defining the biological basis for sex-biased neuropsychiatric risk will depend on purposeful integration of genetic and functional multi-omic datasets within a framework that incorporates established and developing principles of sex-differential neurobiology.
